thread:
zoe_re: Heads-up 1 NorthHarbor is asking for a partner-hosted pilot. They want: partner-side telemetry into Splunk, options for BYOK on Dedicated, and simple chargeback SKUs. Can we triage? :spiral_calendar:

omar_se: I can sketch arch + tenant onboarding flow. Quick clarification: will NorthHarbor create separate tenants per end-customer, or will they proxy all traffic through a shared tenant and tag? This affects entitlement mapping.

northharbor_pm: Likely separate tenants for enterprise customers; small customers might be routed under a shared tenant. Ops wants to avoid 500+ downstream connections though.

ben_ops: Ops note: recommended pattern is pooled export with tenant_id tags instead of opening individual ingestion endpoints per customer. Less connections, lower egress. Example Splunk HEC config: 

```
splunk_hec:
  url: https://splunk.northharbor.com:8088/services/collector/event
  token_role: arn:aws:iam::555666777:role/nhb-redwood-export
  include: [tenant_id, model, tokens, latency_ms]
```
Include tenant_id for billing joins.

sara_security: Security checklist: I'll handle the questionnaire. Key asks to expect: KMS BYOK process for Dedicated, proof of encryption at rest, network egress controls, and our SOC2 report. For BYOK we require offline key wrapping step + attestation. I'll draft language.

omar_se: For Dedicated BYOK we support customer-provided CMKs via AWS KMS or HSM-backed key material in Private. Hosted cannot accept external keys for per-tenant encryption, but we can provide partner-level export with partner's KMS pulling data. I'll diagram both paths.

zoe_re: Pricing ask from NorthHarbor: they want a flat per-tenant monthly fee for small customers and a per-token p95 metric for enterprise testers. Can we propose: SKU-A (hosted): $X per 1M tokens; SKU-B (dedicated): $Y reserved/month + $Z per-peak-token overage. Omar, include SKU examples.

ben_ops: Autoscale + reservation example we'll include in runbook: 

```
capacity:
  reserved_gpu_slots: 60
  burst_capacity_pct: 40
  burst_cooldown_s: 180
```
Callout: burst latency SLO may degrade by ~20ms for bursted requests.

northharbor_pm: Timeline constraints: legal wants SCC answers in 72h, ops wants sample telemetry payload and runbook in 48h to validate billing. Can you confirm?

sara_security: Confirming SCC answers in 72h. I'll attach a KMS policy template and pen-test attestation. Also note: telemetry payloads must be scrubbed of any PII prior to export. We'll provide a sanitizer lambda snippet.

omar_se: Sample telemetry payload (JSON) for Splunk ingestion: 

```
{
  "nh_tenant": "nh-enterprise-77",
  "req": "r-9a3c",
  "model_name": "redwood-opt-8",
  "token_count": 1200,
  "p95_latency_ms": 210,
  "ts": "2026-03-22T18:02:10Z",
  "note": "billing-hook"
}
```
Use "nh_tenant" as join key.

ben_ops: Blocker to flag: if partner requests per-tenant BYOK for hosted tier, that's not supported. We'll offer a hybrid: hosted + partner-export + BYOK for Dedicated. Add that to runbook and commercial note.

sara_security: Adding sanitizer example (lambda pseudocode): 

```
function sanitize(payload) {
  delete payload.user_email;
  if (payload.user_text) payload.user_text = redactPII(payload.user_text);
  return payload;
}
```

Also adding minimum TLS ciphers and rotation cadence in the questionnaire answers.

deploy-bot: CI: telemetry-proxy:v2.1 deployed to staging by omar_se (build 2026.03.22-910).

zoe_re: Action items: Omar -> arch diagram + runbook (48h), Ben -> autoscale/pricing knobs + ops notes (48h), Sara -> SCC answers + KMS template (72h). I'll consolidate and schedule a 30m partner kickoff for next Wednesday. :white_check_mark:

northharbor_pm: Thank you 64F we'll prep legal intake and share partner constraints.

omar_se: Uploading initial runbook draft -> https://redwood.internal/s/northharbor-runbook (will update after review).

sara_security: Uploaded SCC answers -> https://redwood.internal/security/northharbor-scc. Marked BYOK/critical items.

zoe_re: Closing for now, please ping here when artifacts posted and i'll set meeting time.
